light_description: 1995-origin Japanese handmade distortion with wide EQ and heavy sustain; later official Retronics-era documentation preserves the model as a core Drive Breaker identity.
1995-origin overdrive with wide EQ and a more open, lower-gain character than DB-1; official documentation preserves both original and later S-series lineage.
Drive Breaker family overdrive documented in the Retronics catalog; retained as a distinct historical model.
Limited original Drive Breaker multi-channel model sold in 2006; DB-4R is the later reproduction/refinement and preserves the original family identity.
2006 DB-4 reproduction/refinement with DB1R, DB2R, ODB-1 and booster channels; official page documents lineage and exterior pedal record.
Bass-specific Drive Breaker with wide EQ, strong boost and active/passive pickup matching switch.
1995-origin germanium fuzz reissued with the same circuit board/transistor specification; official page documents Bright/Fat switching and exterior imagery.
1995-origin silicon fuzz reissued with documented original circuit/transistors and low-end focused character.
Improved FB-3 successor with fuzz/octave-fuzz switching, noise gate and sustain/gain control; official page documents the model and exterior image.
Compact S-series evolution of DB-1 with modified gain/EQ/noise behavior; official page dates production end to April 2018.
Compact S-series evolution of DB-2 with modified gain/EQ/noise behavior; official page notes a limited quantity rerelease in April 2024 after earlier discontinuation.
Compact S-series overdrive derived from the DB-4R ODB-1 channel; official page documents its transparent, touch-sensitive drive character.
Clean booster evolved from the DB-4R booster channel; retained outside central dirt because primary function is boost.
A/B switch-system utility, not a dirt pedal; retained for builder catalog context only.
